_note: Narration (N*) and Mira's lines (M*) for the demo cut. Mira's lines are her real on-screen questions, re-voiced with her agent voice because the screen recordings captured only the mic.

lines.text: [calmly] Sabine has booked supplier invoices for twenty-four years. On Friday, she retires.
On Monday, Lena starts. The written process covers maybe half of what Sabine actually does.
This is Tacet. Its apprentice is called Mira.
Mira has two jobs: learn from an expert, then teach the next person. Here, Shubham plays Sabine.
Mira watches the real app, and writes down her guess before every decision. The 2019 process says 4711. Sabine books 0400.
[gently] You coded invoice 4471 to 0400 instead of 4711. What made you do that?
She only asks when she's surprised, and only at a pause. The answer is compiled into a rule she can test: equipment over five thousand net is capex.
Is there anything you'd never post without, or a moment where you'd stop and ask someone?

[firmly] But words aren't proof. Mira answers invoices she has never seen, and seals every answer with a hash before anyone labels it. In a live run: nine of eleven, the threshold moved, then eleven of eleven.
Everything lands in a Work Map. Every rule is linked to the expert's own words, and the moment on screen.
An agent takes the same sealed test before it may act alone. And when two experts disagree, Mira shows exactly where, and who to ask.
Monday. Lena books a hydraulic press, codes it to capex, and reaches for Post.
[warmly] Sabine would stop here. Why do you think? Her rule: hold a capex booking until asset accounting provides an asset number.
And it isn't tied to one workflow. On a support desk it had never seen, Mira learned the task from a few demonstrations, and started asking her own questions.
